items.title: The first Koszul homology of a sequence with flat quotient maps onto its base change
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is a base change statement for the first Koszul homology: if B over A is a ring map, f_1 to f_r is a sequence in B whose quotient B/(f_1, ..., f_r) is flat over A, and A to A' is any ring map, then the canonical map from H_1 of the Koszul complex of the sequence tensored with A' to H_1 of the Koszul complex of the base changed sequence is surjective (statement lines 7934-7945). The proof is a 42-line exactness computation (proof lines 7948-7989): it splits the four-term complex wedge^2(B^r) to B^r to B to B/J to 0 into three short exact sequences, tensors them with A' and uses flatness of B/J to keep the first one exact, then deduces J' = J tensor A' and the surjectivity of K tensor A' onto the kernel of the base changed map, and finally identifies H_1 tensor A' with a cokernel that maps onto the cokernel computing H'_1, which is the surjectivity asserted. The single place where the flatness hypothesis is consumed is the exactness of the first tensored sequence, and no step is left to the reader.
